excerpt: Multimodal intelligence can be viewed as human-guided co-evolution between worlds and agents through interaction. However, scaling this process faces two bottlenecks: constructing heterogeneous, verifiable environments is costly, and manual Harness iteration cannot keep pace with growing task diversity and complexity. A key insight is that tasks with different modalities and surface forms can share the same underlying capability requirements. We therefore introduce The Trinity, a recursive self-improvement framework coupling world generation with Harness evolution through three roles: Creator, Explorer, and Evolver. Drawing on verified execution trajectories, Evolver shifts the basis of…

ai.summary: The Trinity introduces a capability‑driven recursive self‑improvement loop for multimodal agents, sharing underlying capabilities across tasks to reduce the cost of building heterogeneous environments.
ai.why: Provides a framework for scaling agent training without manually crafting each new task environment.

title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
excerpt: Recent test-time training (TTT) frameworks have enabled open-weight large language models (LLMs) to outperform inference-only frameworks powered by frontier models on scientific discovery tasks. However, TTT introduces additional computational cost for online weight updates during the discovery process, making computational efficiency an important consideration when scaling to larger models. This motivates us to explore an efficient test-time adaptation method for scientific discovery. We introduce Test-Time Memory Evolution (TTME), a plug-and-play test-time adaptation method, as an alternative to TTT. TTME continually updates the external memory by distilling the experience to guide…

ai.summary: The authors propose a test‑time adaptation method that evolves model memory instead of updating weights, aiming to improve scientific discovery tasks with lower computational cost than test‑time training.
ai.why: Offers a more efficient way to adapt LLMs during inference for discovery workflows.

title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
excerpt: Video captioning aims to preserve visual information through compact descriptions, predominantly using natural language. However, precisely expressing fine-grained spatial structures and temporal dynamics in natural language often leads to lengthy and potentially ambiguous descriptions. In this work, we explore Code as Video Caption, a paradigm where executable programs serve as a complementary representation of visual content through graphical primitives, layout rules, and functions of time. To examine whether code captions effectively preserve video information, we compare them with natural language captions on downstream question answering and video reconstruction tasks. Our results show…

ai.summary: CodeCap‑Bench proposes using executable code as video captions, representing spatial and temporal details with graphical primitives and functions rather than natural language.
ai.why: Offers a new evaluation benchmark for developers interested in code‑based visual representations and multimodal grounding.

title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
excerpt: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. ai.summary: PDRVLA adds a lightweight Physical Dynamics Module that extracts physical tokens from vision‑language features, enabling action generation without costly online video prediction.
ai.why: Allows faster robot control loops while still accounting for dynamics, useful for real‑time robotics applications.

title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
excerpt: Interactive world generation requires models to follow successive commands while preserving relevant history and action consequences. We present Hy-Nomas, a video world model with an 8B diffusion backbone that supports free-form text instructions and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns. It generates variable-length segments conditioned on current inputs and cached history. Our central design aligns structured video captions with action-aware causal attention: descriptive context remains accessible across segments, while action instructions are restricted to their intended temporal windows. A vision-language Prompt Enhancer (PE) translates user requests and multimodal…

ai.summary: Hy‑Nomas is an 8B‑parameter diffusion‑based video world model that supports free‑form text commands and continuous camera control across multiple interaction turns, preserving history via action‑aware causal attention.
ai.why: Enables developers to build interactive video generation systems that respond to sequential user inputs.

title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
excerpt: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have made substantial progress in robotic manipulation, but their generalization remains constrained by the diversity and coverage of action-labeled robot demonstrations. Human videos provide much broader behavioral and environmental experience, while learning from them faces a fundamental trade-off between scalable data and explicit action grounding. We introduce ThinkWorld, a VLA learning framework that grounds action reasoning in world dynamics and strengthens it through reinforcement learning with world imagination. ThinkWorld represents each action thought as a Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD), a sequence of discrete motion tokens that captures the…

ai.summary: ThinkWorld grounds Vision‑Language‑Action learning in world dynamics by using human video data and a chain‑of‑dynamics reasoning approach to improve generalization.
ai.why: Provides a method for developers to leverage large, unlabelled video corpora for more robust robot manipulation models.

title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
excerpt: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. We observe that critic values vary primarily across turns, motivating optimization anchored at turns with finer credit allocation among tokens. We propose Multiscale Policy Optimization (MPO), combining Multiscale Advantage Estimation (MAE) and turn-level importance sampling to align credit assignment and policy updates at the turn scale. Extensive experiments across search, tool-use, and automation tasks with 4B and 30B-A3B models demonstrate consistent gains over strong RL baselines.

ai.summary: The paper introduces Multiscale Policy Optimization (MPO), which combines Multiscale Advantage Estimation and turn‑level importance sampling to improve credit assignment for long‑horizon LLM agents.
ai.why: Provides a new training technique developers of autonomous agents can adopt to boost performance on extended tasks.

title: MatAnyone-E: Sparse Memory Propagation for Efficient High-Resolution Video Matting
excerpt: High-resolution video matting requires preserving fine details, such as hair strands and soft transparency, while maintaining consistency across frames. Memory-based methods achieve strong matting quality by matching current-frame features with information stored from earlier frames, but this process becomes increasingly costly as resolution grows. We present MatAnyone-E, an efficient extension of MatAnyone 2 that focuses computation where it is most needed. Our approach first performs low-resolution propagation to identify uncertain regions that require closer inspection and the memory candidates most relevant to them. It then performs high-resolution matching only for these regions using…

ai.summary: MatAnyone‑E extends the MatAnyone 2 video matting model by first processing low‑resolution frames to guide high‑resolution matting, reducing computation while maintaining detail for high‑resolution video matting.
ai.why: Provides a more efficient high‑resolution matting solution that can be integrated into video pipelines.

title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
excerpt: Action-conditioned world models offer a scalable alternative to costly real-world interaction for improving robot policies. However, existing world-model-based methods largely treat world models as forward-only surrogates of the physical environment, leaving untapped a capability no physical environment affords: rewinding to past decision points to explore counterfactual futures. We introduce Rollback, a policy improvement paradigm that turns world models from passive simulators into counterfactual engines: it rolls back to critical decision points, branches into alternative actions, and contrasts their outcomes to attribute success to individual decisions. This concentrates imagination…

ai.summary: Rollback introduces a policy‑improvement paradigm that rewinds world‑model simulations to past decision points, exploring counterfactual futures to improve robot policies.
ai.why: Gives developers a way to leverage simulated backtracking for more sample‑efficient policy learning.

title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
excerpt: Memory is increasingly used in long-horizon agents, yet the net value of building memory over direct retrieval from raw history remains largely unclear. Taking RAG as a reference, we dissect the net value of memory into the gains and losses over direct retrieval, termed memory benefit and memory tax. These gains and losses arise because memory process changes how the raw information is organized and accessed. We view such changes as the double-edged deviations from the raw history. ai.summary: The paper evaluates long‑horizon agent memory systems across benchmarks and finds many dedicated memory architectures perform worse than simple retrieval‑augmented generation, defining the concepts of memory benefit and memory tax.

title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
excerpt: Can AI agents autonomously train useful language models and improve them using feedback from users? We evaluate their models on 20 benchmarks and through blind human evaluations. All ten agents produce working assistants, with the strongest model, trained by GPT-6 Astra…

title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
excerpt: Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a rule-consistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events. Its 239 self-contained tasks in English and Chinese span 12 categories, from data stories and music-driven pieces to classroom lessons and paper explainers; each asks an agent, running in its native harness inside a sandbox with no image or video generation model, to deliver a finished MP4 with sound…

title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization
excerpt: Video stylization typically transforms entire scenes, while local artistic editing requires precise region--style association, spatial control, and temporal consistency. At its core, GRNStyle builds on Generative Refinement Networks (GRN) and introduces a polar style-aware mask that embeds style identities as equal-norm directions within selected regions. Complementary representation--geometry conditioning combines encoded mask features with raw-mask spatial support, integrating spatiotemporal context with…

ai.summary: LociArt introduces a framework that lets users specify regions and styles for local video stylization using a polar style‑aware mask within a Generative Refinement Network, preserving non‑target content and temporal consistency.
ai.why: Enables developers to build fine‑grained video editing tools with controllable artistic effects.

excerpt: Discrete visual tokens represent vision in a discrete form analogous to language, offering a native interface for multimodal modeling under a shared next-token prediction objective. Using multimodal understanding as a proxy for semantic fidelity, we revisit this assumption and find quantization error unreliable, as discrete representations with substantially larger errors can achieve better understanding. title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
excerpt: Training a spatial VLM to answer which side an object lies on does not require it to preserve the metric displacement that determines that answer, while supervision for a distance estimate may leave categorical relations largely unconstrained. When post-training emphasizes one readout, improvements can therefore concentrate on that interface while transfer to others remains weak or even degrades; we call this observed specialization interface lock-in. ChronoReplay addresses it by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision as chronologically ordered episodes, retaining source-native targets, and balancing supervision across families. Under the same observation access, a single ChronoReplay…

ai.summary: ChronoReplay proposes replaying heterogeneous training data during post‑training to prevent interface lock‑in, where a spatial VLM improves on one answer type (e.g., side classification) at the expense of others like distance estimation.
ai.why: Helps developers build more balanced multimodal models that retain multiple spatial reasoning abilities.

title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
excerpt: In long-term interactions with large language model (LLM) agents, users reveal habits through their choices and actions. We introduce HABIT-Bench to evaluate how well agent memory systems infer habits from weak evidence and apply them to later requests. ai.summary: HABIT‑Bench evaluates how well agent memory systems infer and apply user habits from sparse, longitudinal evidence across conversations.

title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception

title: Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI
excerpt:
Modern engineering projects increasingly combine human judgment with machine capability. An engineer can define a problem, then ask an artificial intelligence tool to search relevant research and technical standards, generate design options, test them in simulation, and compare the results. The engineer can then bring the results to specialists who understand the parts AI cannot judge on its own, such as whether a design can be built safely, whether it makes sense in a particular setting, or how it might affect its users. The final decision about whether and how to move forward remains a human responsibility.
AI can help engineers do early project steps that once required several people…

ai.summary: IEEE Spectrum argues that modern engineering projects combine human judgment with AI tools for research, design generation, simulation, and comparison, but still require human specialists for safety, feasibility, and contextual decisions.
ai.why: Highlights the complementary role of AI in engineering workflows and the ongoing need for human oversight.
